problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE methods (Open-Nav, SmartWay, EvoNav) rely on trained waypoint predictors that restrict the VLM's action space and hide depth. Memory is handled by accumulating long prompt histories full of irrelevant context, or by retrieving cross-episode experience, which breaks the zero-shot assumption.
motivation: The VLM-environment interface, not just the reasoning model, limits zero-shot navigation. A predictor that fails to propose an instruction-relevant direction makes that goal unreachable, and it generalizes poorly sim-to-real. Exposing action, depth and memory as on-demand tools lets the VLM use its visual reasoning freely.
key_idea: Treat zero-shot VLN-CE as tool calling: the VLM picks target pixels directly (move_to), queries metric depth only where needed (query_depth), and recalls past observations selectively (recall) via a map image, with no trained waypoint predictor.
insight: Directly selecting pixels beats a learned waypoint predictor (SR 55 vs 50 when the predictor replaces the Action Tool). Structured depth queries beat both no depth (42) and depth images added to the input (53). Selective recall adds value beyond a map-only memory (51 vs 55), and removing all agentic memory drops SR to 41. Both memory and depth interfaces matter, and the harness helps even weaker backbones (Qwen3.6-27B reaches 35% SR).
method: Agentic tool interface: the VLM sees N heading-indexed RGB views, a map image and the tool history; it can issue multiple tool calls per step from {query_depth, recall, move_to, stop}. query_depth and recall return evidence, while move_to and stop end the step.

Depth Tool query_depth: takes a batch of (view, u, v) normalized pixels and returns metric depth, 5x5 neighbourhood min/mean/median, and an action preview (relative yaw, executable distance). Raw depth maps are never shown to the VLM.
Agentic Memory and Recall Tool: within-episode memory holds a compact trajectory map image (always in the prompt) and a bounded cache of past images, which recall(p,k) returns on demand.

Action Tool move_to(k,u,v): back-projects the selected pixel with depth, intrinsics and the view-to-agent transform. It computes the bearing and an executable distance after a stopping margin, max-step clipping and step discretization.

Safety check: rejects out-of-range targets, invalid depth and too-short motions. It also rejects any motion whose swept corridor contains body-height obstacle points from the back-projected depth, returning Reselect; otherwise it executes.
Real-world deployment: an omnidirectional four-wheel robot with RealSense D435 RGB-D, LiDAR and FAST-LIO; multi-view observations (1 or 4 views) are collected by rotating in place.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.5 (frozen, main); also Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-3-Flash, MiMo-V2.5, Qwen3.6-27B
setting.observation: multi-view (panoramic) RGB-D, heading-indexed; the VLM sees only RGB plus tool-returned depth values
setting.action_space: continuous (turn θ, forward distance ρ) from a VLM-selected pixel, with a geometric safety check

numbers.eval_set_note: 30 real-world episodes: lab, office, outdoor yard

results: On the 100-episode R2R-CE val-unseen protocol, AgenticNav-GPT-5.5 reaches 55 SR / 48.41 SPL, versus 44 / 35.04 for the same-backbone SmartWay reproduction. It also beats EvoNav-Gemini-2.5-pro in SR (49 vs 43 with Gemini-2.5-Pro), though its SPL and nDTW are lower there. In the real world it doubles SmartWay's SR (46.7% vs 23.3%) with 4 views.
limitations: Failures are dominated by VLM decision errors (88.9% in simulation, 71.4% in the real world); API timeouts and planning/control failures account for the rest of the real-world failures.

Evaluation covers only 100 R2R-CE episodes and 30 real-world episodes, so the results are small-sample. Relies on large proprietary VLMs (GPT-5.5), which brings latency and API dependence; smaller models reach much lower SR.
Not compared against strong supervised methods on SR (BEVBert reaches 60), and the SPL/nDTW of the Gemini-2.5-Pro variant trail EvoNav.
